1.pericope_label: Against Moab: Nebo spoiled, Heshbon plotted against, and weeping the whole way up the ascent of Luhith
debates: Whether the heading reads against Moab or concerning Moab
Whether Misgab is a proper name at all
Whether the little ones are cities or children
outliers: Ellicott makes the little ones cities on the strength of the name Zoar, and Calvin expressly rejects that reading for children
Calvin denies the upper and lower Horonaim that Gill reports from Kimchi and Ben Melech
themes: A prophecy against kinsmen rather than aliens
Names that pun on the doom pronounced over them
A boast about a city that had changed hands twice
Grief too great for fear or shame to check

6.pericope_label: Flee and be like the heath in the wilderness: Chemosh into captivity, and a curse on the sword kept back from blood
debates: Whether the summons to flee is counsel or irony
What the works Moab trusted in were
Whether the curse of the tenth verse is addressed to the Chaldeans or is a general rule for all service done for God
outliers: Calvin says the common application of the tenth verse to all work done for God absurdly misrepresents it, and Gill expounds it in exactly that way
Keil and Delitzsch deny that Aroer can be a town in the sixth verse, where Clarke and Calvin both think a city is meant
themes: A shrub in the desert as the picture of a nation
A god carried into exile with his own priests
Confidence divided between fortresses and idols
A curse pronounced on mercy in war

11.pericope_label: Moab settled on his lees: tilters sent to empty his vessels, and Chemosh shamed as Bethel was
debates: Whether resting on the lees improves wine or leaves it crude
What the wanderers of the twelfth verse are
Whom the comparison with Bethel is aimed at
outliers: Ellicott says wine left on its lees keeps its first crude bitterness, where Clarke and Calvin say the lees preserve and improve it; Keil and Delitzsch divide the case between good wine and inferior
themes: Long peace named as a reason for judgment
A nation compared to a cask never racked
Discipline found in defeat and exile
A warning aimed past its stated target

14.pericope_label: How say ye, We are mighty: the chosen young men gone down to the slaughter, and the strong staff broken
debates: Whether the verb of the fifteenth verse describes the spoiler coming up or the people going away
Whether the call to bemoan Moab asks for real sympathy
How long a delayed threatening remains credible
outliers: Henry says it is more useful to be possessed with awe than to enquire critically into the figures, which is the very work Calvin and Keil and Delitzsch are doing on the same verses
Gill reads the summons to bemoan as a real call on the neighbouring nations, where Calvin denies that any pity is intended by it
themes: Confidence answered before the sentence is out
Prophecy spoken in the past tense for certainty
A promise held as present though the fulfilment is remote
A sceptre named only at the moment it breaks

18.pericope_label: Come down from thy glory, daughter of Dibon: Aroer questioning the fugitives, and judgment on the plain country
debates: What sitting in thirst means
Which of the two towns called Aroer is addressed
Whether the situation of the listed cities is worth investigating
outliers: Calvin says it would be useless labour to determine where the listed cities stood, which is precisely the work Ellicott and Keil and Delitzsch undertake on the same verses
Wesley takes the name at the twentieth verse for a river, and Clarke and Gill treat it as a place where news is to be told
themes: A city rich in water threatened with thirst
A frontier town told to interrogate the refugees
Grammar shifting to show a rout rather than a march
Threatenings driven in like nails because they would not be believed

22.pericope_label: Judgment upon all the cities of Moab far or near: the horn cut off, and the boaster made to wallow in his vomit
debates: Where Kerioth and the Moabite Bozrah stood
Whether the vomit of the twenty-sixth verse means grief or intemperate joy
Whether the list reaches beyond the plain country north of the Arnon
outliers: Ellicott reports an identification of Kerioth and Bozrah sixty miles north of Heshbon, which others think fatal to it, and a rival identification close to Dibon
Calvin records a reading that turns the vomit into past exultation before setting it aside for the received sense of grief
themes: Town names read for the meanings buried in them
A list closed with the words far and near
Strength figured as a horn and then as an arm
A cup poured out by human hands at divine command

27.pericope_label: Was not Israel a derision unto thee: Moab sent to the rock like a dove, and the pride of Moab reported
debates: Whether the question about thieves clears Israel or admits her guilt
Who speaks the words we have heard
Whether the command to dwell in the rock is counsel or sentence
outliers: Ellicott reports critics who read the particle as when, making the verse concede that Israel had been an unjust invader, against his own reading that it clears her
Gill sets aside Kimchi, who makes the nations the speakers of the twenty-ninth verse, in favour of God himself
themes: A nation punished for the way it received another nation ruin
Wrong done to the Church counted as done to God
Fugitives told to nest like doves in the cliffs
Boasting loud enough to be called a bellowing

30.pericope_label: I know his wrath: howling for Moab and for the men of Kir-heres, and the spoiler fallen on the vine of Sibmah
debates: What the second clause of the thirtieth verse means
Who is speaking when the howling begins
What the name Kir-heres means
outliers: Calvin gives the name Kir-heres as the city of potsherd, where Ellicott takes it for the City of the Sun and connects it with nature-worship
Calvin rejects the rendering of the disputed word as sons on the ground that the chapter promises Moab a remnant
themes: A verse whose obscurity every voice concedes
A lament with no agreed speaker
A vineyard measured out by the weeping it will cost
Ground still fruitful under a sentence of ruin

33.pericope_label: Joy taken from the plentiful field: a cry from Heshbon to Horonaim, and an end of him that burneth incense
debates: What the repeated shouting word means
Whether the heifer of three years old is a place name, a figure of wantonness, or a figure of distress
Where the waters of Nimrim were
outliers: Calvin sets down a reason for the heifer comparison that he calls more suitable to the passage than the one he has just given
Ellicott reports critics who resolve the heifer into a proper name and a triple city, and answers that no such town is known
themes: A harvest song named only to be cancelled
Two towns close enough to hear each other scream
A figure that may mean either wantonness or thirst
Worship ended by deporting the priests

36.pericope_label: Mine heart shall sound for Moab like pipes: every head bald, and Moab broken like a vessel wherein is no pleasure
debates: Whether the sounding heart is the prophet or the people of Moab
Whether the mourning customs described are to be approved
Why the lamentation is set on the housetops
outliers: Ellicott takes the prophet to be speaking his own grief, where Gill reports Kimchi and Calvin agrees with him that the prophet is impersonating the Moabites
Calvin condemns as excess and hypocrisy the very mourning signs that Gill, Clarke, Ellicott and Keil and Delitzsch record without comment
themes: A heart that sounds like a funeral pipe
Grief carried past what nature warrants
Roofs turned from places of prayer into places of panic
A vessel nobody wants, against children still held precious

40.pericope_label: He shall fly as an eagle: the strongholds surprised, and fear and the pit and the snare upon Moab
debates: Whether Kerioth is a place name or means simply the cities
Whether Moab ceased to be a people for a time or for ever
What the spreading of the wings signifies
outliers: Clarke doubts that Moab was ever reinstated as a nation, against Gill, who reads the destruction as temporary because the chapter closes by promising a return
Calvin denies that the spread wings carry any sense of shelter, which is their usual force in the figure
themes: An invader flying at a nation that had been told to nest in cliffs
Courage described as a gift needing daily renewal
Three words for one hunt with no way out of it
Delay explained as timing rather than neglect

45.pericope_label: A fire out of Heshbon: woe unto Moab, the people of Chemosh, and yet a captivity to be brought again
debates: What the word rendered because of the force belongs to
What the fire out of Heshbon stands for
Whether the promised return is literal, spiritual, or both
outliers: Calvin sets aside the majority reading of the fire as the coming spoiler, and makes the two cities themselves the place where the fire is kindled
Clarke denies any literal restoration of Moab, where Gill dates one under Cyrus and cites Josephus for the nation surviving into later times
themes: A refuge that turns out to be the source of the fire
A single cry doing the work of a long lament
Judgment closing with a clause of mercy
A formula that may be the mark of a copyist rather than a prophet
